questions.text: In national accounting, the difference between the domestic goods produced for a given year and the domestic goods purchased for a given year is equal to:

options.c: The difference between gross domestic product and net domestic product
options.d: The difference between real GDP and nominal GDP

questions.text: GDP per capita is indeed an imperfect measure of a given population's well-being, but it is wrong to claim that:

options.a: GDP per capita does not take into account the pollution level of the output activities
options.b: GDP per capita is uncorrelated to the health of the considered population
options.c: GDP per capita ignores the distribution of income
options.d: GDP per capita does not capture the contribution of activities happening in the private sphere (i.e. not being the subject of a market transaction) to added value creation

questions.text: The demand for reserves by commercial banks is:

options.a: Independent from the way agents allocate their money demand between currency and checkable deposits
options.b: Increasing along the demand for checkable deposits
options.c: Independent from the aggregate price level in the considered economy
options.d: Increasing along the demand for currency

questions.text: The IS-LM model assumes that the production factors are underemployed. This means:

options.a: That a decrease in the size of the labor force might have no effect on the equilibrium activity level
options.b: That increasing the public deficit level is always relevant when trying to counteract the impact of a negative demand shock
options.c: That increasing investment might have no effect on the equilibrium activity level
options.d: None of the above answers is correct

questions.text: In the IS-LM model without expectations and in a closed economy:

options.a: A variation of the tax level impacts private consumption and leads the equilibrium to move along the IS curve
options.b: A variation of investments due to a variation in the interest rate level leads the equilibrium to move along the IS curve
options.c: A variation of private consumption due to a variation in the interest rate level leads to a shift of the IS curve
options.d: A variation in the level of public expenditures leads the equilibrium to move along the IS curve

questions.text: In a fiscal expansion context, if the Central Bank wants to maintain the interest rate at its objective level i, it has to:

options.a: Sell securities on the financial markets
options.b: Buy securities on the financial markets
options.d: Carry out the necessary actions so as to maintain the money supply at a constant level

questions.text: (Select the incorrect answer among the propositions below) In the IS-LM model, an increase in the tax level leads to:

options.a: A shift in the IS curve
options.b: A decrease in the private consumption level following the decrease in available income
options.c: A decrease in the public deficit
options.d: An increase in the equilibrium interest rate on the monetary market

questions.text: In the IS-LM model, at the equilibrium on the market for goods and services:

options.a: private savings are equal to investment
options.b: for a given level of public savings, a decrease in private savings leads to an increase in the investment level
options.c: for a given investment level, an increase in the public deficit implies a decrease in private savings
options.d: when public expenditures are higher than taxes, private savings exceed investment

questions.text: (Select the incorrect answer among the propositions below) The "discouraged workers":

options.a: are part of the labor force
options.b: have given up looking for a job
options.d: are part of the working-age population

options.a: the share of the working-age population that does not work
options.b: the share of people looking for a job within the working-age population
options.c: the share of the labor force that does not work
options.d: the share of people looking for a job in the population

questions.text: In the AS-AD model framework, and considering an economy in which the output level is currently below the natural activity level, an expansive monetary policy:

options.a: Is uncalled for, since it drives the price level up without any impact on output in the short run
options.b: Is relevant so as to avoid a deflationary trend, but had no effect on output in the short run
options.c: Is uncalled for, since it has no impact on the price level and the output level in the short run
options.d: Is relevant so as to stimulate output in the short run and avoid a deflationary trend

questions.text: In the graphical representation of the AS-AD model, there is a point where the output level is equal to the natural output level, and where the observed prices are equal to the expected prices.

options.a: This point is always at the intersection of the AS and the AD curves
options.b: This point is always on the AD curve, and sometimes on the AS curve
options.c: This point is always on the AS curve, and sometimes on the AD curve
options.d: It is possible that after a macroeconomic shock, this point is temporarily neither on the AS nor on the AD curve

options.a: The behaviour of economic agents is not affected by the implemented macroeconomic policies
options.b: Taking expectations into account necessarily implies a negative fiscal multiplier in the case of a fiscal consolidation
options.c: Agents' expectations are not independent from changes in macroeconomic policies
options.d: At each period, agents correct their expectations from a fraction of the error observed for the previous period

questions.text: In the IS-LM model with expectations:

options.a: The impact of an expansive monetary policy on economic activity will necessarily be smaller than predicted by the IS-LM model without expectations
options.b: The impact of a restrictive fiscal policy on economic activity will necessarily be smaller than predicted by the IS-LM model without expectations
options.c: The impact of an expansive monetary policy on economic activity will necessarily be stronger than predicted by the IS-LM model without expectations
options.d: None of the above answers are correct

questions.text: The IS curve is steeper in the IS-LM model with expectations because:

options.a: At a given expectations level, a variation in the current real interest rate has a limited impact on the present value of future income
options.b: At a given expectations level, a variation in the current output has a stronger impact on the present value of future income
options.c: investment is more volatile than private consumption
options.d: the present value of future income depends on the real interest rate and not the nominal one
